sections.overview: Tipula paludosa is a crane fly whose larvae, known as leatherjackets, live in soil and can damage grass and crops.
sections.identification: The adult is a long-legged fly; the legless, grey-brown larva is the stage most often noticed for its feeding damage.
sections.habitat: It is associated with moist soils, including grassland and turf; its range includes northern Europe and introduced areas.
sections.diet: The larvae are polyphagous and feed on plant material, including roots and the bases of grasses.
sections.behavior: It usually has one generation per year; adults fly mainly in late summer and autumn, while larvae feed during the cooler months.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted describe an annual life cycle but provide limited species-specific detail on mating and egg laying.
sections.ecology: Unlike the related Tipula oleracea, which can have two generations in a year, T. paludosa is generally univoltine; their seasonal activity can help distinguish them.
sections.conservation: The consulted agricultural and natural-history sources discuss its range and occasional pest damage but give no global conservation assessment.
